newsitem.title: GERMANY: Arthuis says satisfied with current forex levels.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says satisfied with current forex levels.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Saturday he was satisfied with current foreign exchange rate levels, following discussions by finance ministers and central bank chiefs at the Group of Seven (G7) meeting.
Arthuis also said he hoped any country not taking part in European currency union at its proposed start date in 1999 will be able to join as soon as possible.
Bank of France Governor Jean-Claude Trichet also said a clear consensus had emerged at the G7 meeting in Berlin about currency markets.
"The consensus is clear -- orderly consolidation at a level judged to be satisfying by all the participants," Trichet told a news conference.
Arthuis said he welcomed developments on foreign exchange markets. "What we must do is consolidate and ensure that these rates are stable," he said.
"The situation on exchange rates today is satisfying. That is the consensus of the G7," he added.
Last autumn, France was among the most vocal in calling for a dollar rise, and there had been some speculation that it would like to see it climb further.
Arthuis said, however, that the misalignments in currencies seen two years ago "have been corrected."
He said European countries had also briefed their G7 partners about decisions taken at a European summit in Dublin in December on monetary union.

He declined to comment on reported tensions between Germany, which many believe would like membership of monetary union restricted initially to a hard core of northern European countries, and Italy, which along with Spain and Portugal, wants to join at the euro's launch in January 1999.
He noted that a decision would be taken in early 1998 on which countries were eligible to join in 1999.
"We must hope that anyone who is not in the first group can join as quickly as possible," he said.
